summary: An unknown render view prints a stack after build outputs change. The T2 test bypasses fixture ownership and can test the wrong checkout. The shared runner did not start the independent runtime checks.
blocking_findings: C-P2-1 [Blocker] review-c: An unknown render view prints a stack instead of one error line. src/cli/forge.ts:405 validates the view after lines 327–341 change build outputs. Lines 715–729 print the stack. Validate render views before the build and report the known-view list without the stack.

C-P2-2 [Blocker] review-c: tests/render-options.test.ts:64–69 and :192–194 bypass exclusive creation when the actual fixture path exists. The render then uses the pre-existing asset instead of reporting the required collision. The probe at :202–214 writes with no exclusive flag and can replace and remove a pre-existing probe. Use one ownership check and cover collision on the actual fixture path.

C-P2-3 [Blocker] review-c: tests/render-options.test.ts:7–12 and :55–58 hard-code the audit worktree. A test run in another checkout can execute Forge and write fixtures in this worktree instead of verifying its own code. Derive the repository root from the test module.
nonblocking_findings: C-P2-4 [Nit] review-c: src/cli/forge.ts:45–54 says --ortho makes the frame level and --focus zooms every view. src/render/page.ts:432–449 retains the selected elevation and ignores focus under --ortho. State that the level views set elevation and that the fixed frame does not use focus.

C-P2-5 [Nit] review-c: The new camera comments do not explain the side projection sign. At src/cli/forge.ts:113 or src/render/page.ts:443, cite decision (j): the camera looks from +X with +Y up, so image right is -Z.

C-P2-6 [Nit] review-c: plan.md:185–186 says renderViews restores both changes. src/render/page.ts:435–461 resets no camera state; it restores the materials and ground. Name the state that the restore function resets.
evidence: git rev-parse HEAD returned the supplied audited SHA.

A read-only probe of the audited parseArgs options and flat guard produced one line for each invalid flat combination and for the unknown option.
A read-only probe of ensureRendered simulated a pre-existing pin path. It called the render once and the exclusive create zero times.
The read-only AC1 guard passed on the audited HEAD and rejected the phase base. All four titles, three comments, and three active hero names matched.
plan.md:259–274 schedules the durable AC1 guard for T4. tests/sprout-mom-kim.test.ts does not exist on the audited HEAD.
The Phase 2 plan and strategy name no README or docs deliverable. The spec contains both commands at lines 433–442. README.md:207 still lists only the original render options.

The flat-pass JSDoc names the material, visibility, and ground changes. studio.ts:32 keeps sRGB. page.ts:461 restores the materials and ground in finally. Sprite and cut-out requests set their own camera parameters.
Prettier passed on all four T1 and T2 test files. The T2 test names identify the user-visible behavior. The named-view and missing-flag assertions share one case as planned.
Both wrapped invocations reported a shared lock wait over 600 seconds. I stopped my jobs before the CLI or Vitest started. All captured audit processes exited.

The CLI registers both options as long boolean flags. The flags flow through ViewsRequest to the render page. No HTTP route contract changed.
